Checklist Item: UI layout matches approved design mockups/Figma files at desktop and mobile viewports; spacing and alignment within acceptable tolerance (2-4px)
Font weights and styles render correctly across all browsers; text truncation and overflow behavior is intentional and consistent
Brand colors are applied consistently across all pages and components; no off-brand color variants visible
Placeholder and stock images replaced with final brand-approved assets; image and icon style consistent with brand guidelines
Visual hierarchy clearly guides user attention to primary actions and content on each page
Interactive element states (hover; active; disabled; selected) are visually distinct and consistent; disabled states meet WCAG contrast thresholds
Navigation structure is logical and discoverable; users can reach any page within 3 clicks; back button behavior is predictable
Deep linking and URL sharing work correctly; shared URLs render the expected page state
Core user flows (signup; login; purchase; search) are intuitive and require minimal steps to complete
Multi-step processes show clear progress indication and allow backward navigation
Destructive actions (delete; cancel; overwrite) require explicit confirmation with clear consequences explained
Loading states provide appropriate visual feedback (spinners; skeleton screens; progress bars) for operations >300ms
Empty states have meaningful content with guidance on next steps; error recovery paths are clear
Success and failure feedback is timely and visible without requiring user to scroll or search for confirmation
Form validation messaging is clear and specific; tells user exactly what is wrong and how to fix it; inline validation timing is appropriate
Form field order follows logical data entry sequence; tab order matches visual layout
Page transitions feel smooth and responsive; no jarring jumps or flashes between views
Content is free of spelling and grammatical errors across all pages and components
Microcopy (button labels; tooltips; placeholders; helper text) is clear; consistent in tone; and avoids technical jargon for target audience
Content hierarchy guides users through information logically; most important information first
Legal and compliance text (terms of service; privacy policy; disclaimers) is present where required; links are functional and accessible from all pages
Cookie consent meets regional compliance requirements (GDPR; CCPA); user data handling and storage practices comply with applicable privacy regulations
Visual appearance consistent across target browsers (Chrome; Firefox; Safari; Edge); web fonts render consistently with no FOIT or excessive FOUT
JavaScript-dependent features work correctly across all target browsers including Safari and Firefox
Touch interactions work correctly on iOS and Android; touch target sizes meet minimum 44x44px (WCAG 2.5.8); no double-tap-to-zoom interference
Scrolling is smooth on mobile; landscape and portrait orientations handled gracefully without content clipping
Mobile keyboard does not obscure active input field; appropriate keyboard types triggered for different input fields
Layout adapts gracefully at all viewport widths; content reflow between breakpoints maintains logical reading order and visual hierarchy
Images scale without distortion; typography remains readable at all viewport sizes; tables usable on mobile viewports
Navigation adapts appropriately for mobile; mobile navigation overlay does not create accessibility issues and can be closed easily
Screen reader announces page content in logical order; custom interactive components (dropdowns; tabs; accordions) are understandable and operable via screen reader
Dynamic content changes announced appropriately; image alt text accurately conveys meaning; decorative images hidden from screen reader
Cognitive load is appropriate; consistent interaction patterns used throughout; instructions do not rely solely on sensory characteristics
Time-based content and session timeouts provide adequate warnings and options to extend
Information conveyed by color is also conveyed through text labels; patterns; or icons; color choices reviewed with color vision deficiency simulators
Content remains functional and readable at 400% zoom as required by WCAG 2.1 AA Reflow criterion
Above-the-fold content loads and renders within perceptually acceptable time (<2.5s); page transitions feel responsive with no white flashes or layout jumps
Scroll performance is smooth on content-heavy pages; large datasets use appropriate pagination or virtualization
Offline or slow network degrades gracefully; third-party script failures do not block or degrade core page functionality
RTL layout renders correctly for RTL languages; text expansion (up to 200% longer than English) does not break layouts or cause overflow
Date; time; number; currency formats and decimal separators match target locale conventions
Translated content fits within UI containers without clipping; buttons and labels accommodate longer translations
AEM or CMS-specific frontend build tooling configured correctly; webfont loading strategy prevents FOIT in production
Third-party library and framework choices are justified; no redundant libraries serving the same purpose
CSS architecture follows agreed methodology (BEM; ITCSS; utility-first) consistently; component CSS is self-contained without unintended side effects
Component library documentation is complete and up to date; design system tokens in code match latest design specifications
Functions and complex code blocks have descriptive comments explaining purpose and business logic rationale
Component prop interfaces are well-defined; use specific types (not 'any'); and documented with descriptions
Structured data (JSON-LD / Schema.org) is valid and passes Google Rich Results Test for all key page templates
Open Graph meta tags (og:title; og:description; og:image; og:url) present and correct on shareable pages
Sitemap.xml is complete and submitted to search engines; robots.txt configured correctly and does not block important pages
Project management tool set up and actively used; board reflects current sprint work accurately; backlog is groomed and prioritized
Tickets have clear acceptance criteria and priority before development; bug tickets include reproduction steps; severity; and expected vs actual behavior
Definition of Done documented and agreed upon; git commits and PRs reference ticket IDs for traceability from requirement to deployment
Design tool used for all UI work; component library mirrors development library; design tokens synchronized between design and code
Design files include specifications for all viewport breakpoints (mobile; tablet; desktop)
Design-to-development handoff process defined; design QA step exists where designer reviews implemented UI before ticket completion
Branching strategy documented (Git Flow; GitHub Flow; Trunk-Based) and understood by all team members
Release and hotfix processes documented; releases versioned (semantic versioning preferred); hotfixes merge back to both main and develop
Code review checklist documented; reviewers check for functionality; readability; security; performance; and accessibility
Code reviews completed within agreed SLA; feedback is constructive and references coding standards or best practices
QA testing process defined with functional; regression; and exploratory testing; QA environment mirrors production configuration
Cross-browser and device testing matrix defined; target browsers/devices documented and tested before major releases
Accessibility testing included in QA process; UAT or stakeholder sign-off required before production deployment
Release checklist documented and followed; rollback plan documented and tested for deployment revert within defined threshold
Post-deployment monitoring in place (error tracking; performance; uptime); incident response process documented with escalation paths
Technical documentation (architecture decisions; ADRs; system diagrams) maintained and current; onboarding documentation exists for new developers
Technical debt tracked in issue tracker; regularly reviewed and prioritized for remediation
Dependency update policy documented; security patches applied within defined SLA
Secrets management process defined; API keys and credentials stored in vault or environment variables; secret rotation policy in place
GenAI usage policy documented covering approved tools; permitted use cases; data handling restrictions; and code review requirements for AI-generated output
Only licensed and organization-approved GenAI tools used; enterprise tiers used where available for data privacy and IP protection
Confidential source code; customer data; and internal business logic not submitted to public GenAI services without data-privacy safeguards
GenAI usage compliant with client contractual obligations; disclosure provided where contractually required
AI-generated code identified in PRs and undergoes same review rigor as human-written code; reviewers verify logic; edge cases; and security
GenAI tools configured with project-specific context (.cursorrules; copilot-instructions) to align output with project coding standards
Developers understand and can explain all committed code regardless of generation method; no 'black box' code merged
AI-generated documentation reviewed for accuracy; no hallucinated feature descriptions or API references committed without verification
AI-generated code reviewed for IP concerns; no verbatim reproduction of third-party copyrighted code; telemetry and data-sharing settings reviewed
AI-generated UI components reviewed for accessibility compliance; manual verification required for ARIA attributes; keyboard handlers; and semantic HTML
